outcome: cesarean section for failure to progress
cohort: A group of 957 term and late preterm (>=34 weeks) singleton pregnancies with a complete gestational follow-up and an ultrasound examination within 2 weeks of delivery.
finding: Induction of labor was the most important modifiable factor, followed by smoking and maternal weight, while parity was the most important nonmodifiable factor, followed by maternal age and estimated fetal weight, in determining cesarean section for failure to progress.
mod_finding: Induction of labor, smoking, and maternal weight were identified as modifiable factors increasing the incidence of cesarean section for failure to progress.
